mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level (FEDFUNDS) has a negative linear relationship with S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as higher rates compress equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows, leading to negative returns when the rate is elevated.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day forward returns is not negative (rank IC < -0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the average return in high-rate periods (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) is not significantly lower than the average return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 303.0 signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain or increase interest rates, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return when CPIAUCSL > 303.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 5-day returns is below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 303.0) and high interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0) indicates a monetary policy tightening cycle that suppresses equity returns, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when both CPIAUCSL > 303.0 and FEDFUNDS > 5.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC for the joint condition is below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), the labor market is tight, which signals strong economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when UNRATE < 3.5% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC between UNRATE and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1400.0 (thousands) signals weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return when HOUST < 1400.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC between HOUST and 5-day returns is below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in housing starts (HOUST < 1400.0) and retail sales (RSAFS < 680000.0) indicates a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when both HOUST < 1400.0 and RSAFS < 680000.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC for the joint condition is below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 101.0 (index) signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when INDPRO < 101.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC between INDPRO and 20-day returns is below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in total nonfarm employment below 155000.0 (thousands) signals a weakening labor market, which is associated with reduced consumer spending and economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when PAYEMS < 155000.0 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the rank IC between PAYEMS and 60-day returns is below -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
